title: Is Muzz Safe? What We Actually Do About Catfish, Scammers and Harassment
summary: Learn how Muzz combats catfish, scammers, fake profiles and harassment with selfie verification, moderation and privacy features.
body_text: Muzz requires every member to complete selfie verification before they can be seen. Profiles are manually reviewed, blocking and reporting are free and available to everyone, and photo privacy is on by default rather than sold as an upgrade. Muzz has over 10 million members and 800,000 success stories. Looking for your soulmate? You won’t find your soulmate on this blog post but you might find them on Muzz - the world’s biggest Muslim dating and marriage app. Sign Up muzz It’s a fair question, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a paragraph about how much we value your trust. So here is what Muzz actually does, what it doesn’t do, and what you should do yourself – on Muzz or anywhere else. Is Muzz a legitimate app? Muzz is a Muslim marriage app founded in 2015 by our co-founder Shahzad Younas, who left a career at Morgan Stanley, taught himself to code and built the first version of the app himself. It went through Y Combinator, reached its first million users in 2016, and rebranded from Muzmatch to Muzz in 2022. Today Muzz has over 10 million members and more than 800,000 success stories – couples who met on the app and got married. Muzz is independently owned. It has never been sold to a larger dating (Zionist) conglomerate, and its founder has stated publicly and repeatedly that it will not be. Free Palestine forever and always. Does Muzz verify every profile? Yes. Selfie verification is mandatory on Muzz, not an optional badge and not a paid feature. Every member submits a selfie, which is compared against their profile photo to confirm the profile belongs to a real person. That selfie is never shared with anyone – not with other members, not with third parties – and is used only for security. Muzz also reviews profiles manually. Photos that don’t meet the guidelines are rejected, and every member has to show their face in their verification selfie. Manual review is slower than pure automation, and that’s deliberate. Muzz also monitors behaviour, not just profiles. Accounts that like or message at volume – fast, indiscriminate, the pattern of someone working through a list rather than looking for a spouse – get flagged automatically and reviewed by a person. Muzz founder Shahzad Younas has written publicly about how the company approaches this, and he’s blunt about it: it’s a permanent cat-and-mouse game, and he won’t claim it’s solved. (ref: https://x.com/ShahzadYounas_/status/1889686271515058626?s=20 ) Some context from that thread worth repeating: Scammers target relationship apps specifically, because people there are emotionally open and are often too embarrassed to report being defrauded. These aren’t opportunists – Muzz has encountered organised operations running scams as full-time work from dedicated offices. What Muzz uses against them: device identification, selfie and facial-similarity recognition, and further methods the company deliberately doesn’t publish. A significant focus is stopping blocked scammers from simply signing up again – the single measure that most affects whether a removal actually sticks. Muzz tracks how long a suspected scammer exists on the platform before being detected and removed, and that window has narrowed meaningfully as these measures have come in. The goal is removal before the account can match or message anyone at all. Shahzad has also noted the uncomfortable part: AI now makes some deception nearly impossible to spot by eye, which means increasingly using AI to detect AI. Honorable mention: Only women review verification selfies. Muzz’s community team is all women, by design. For sisters who wear hijab or niqab, or who simply don’t want their face reviewed by a man, verification shouldn’t mean a trade-off — so it isn’t one. The selfie you submit is seen by a woman on the Muzz team, and by no one else. It never appears on your profile, is never shown to other members, and is never shared outside Muzz. Are there fake profiles and catfish on Muzz? Any platform with millions of members attracts people acting in bad faith. Pretending otherwise would be the least trustworthy thing an app could do. What Muzz does about it: mandatory selfie verification at signup, manual profile review, and an investigation process for impersonation reports. If you think someone is impersonating another person, report them and Muzz will investigate. How to spot a fake profile One photo, or several that look like the same shot. Real profiles have variety – different settings, different lighting, different days. A bio with nothing specific in it. Generic virtues and no details about their actual life is a signal. They refuse a video call. Muzz has free in-app video calling. Someone serious about marriage will use it. Someone who won’t, after weeks of chatting, is telling you something. They want to move off the app immediately. Wanting your snapchat or WhatsApp within the first few messages usually means they want to be somewhere with no verification, no moderation and no reporting. The story escalates fast. Intense declarations early, then a crisis, then a request. That’s the shape of a romance scam. Money enters the conversation at all. An emergency, an investment opportunity, a visa problem, a gift card. No exceptions, no matter how good the reason sounds. How do you block or report someone on Muzz? Blocking is free, takes seconds, and works two ways. From their profile: open the profile, scroll to the bottom, select Block, choose a reason, submit. From your chat: open the chat, tap the three dots in the top right, and under Safety Options select Block, then confirm. Two things worth knowing, both documented publicly by Muzz: They are not notified. The person you block is never told. It works both ways. They can’t see or message you, and you won’t see them either. Reporting is separate from blocking, and you should do both when someone’s behaviour breaks the rules rather than just being a bad match. Reports go to the moderation team for review, and Muzz operates a ban appeals process so decisions can be contested. What safety resources does Muzz offer? Muzz runs a Safety Center at muzz.com/us/en/safety/ with four sets of published guidelines: Profile Quality Guidelines – what makes a thoughtful, halal profile Behavior guidelines – the standard Muzz expects of members and what breaks it Safety Guidelines – practical advice for using the app safely Safety Resources – external helplines, including Samaritans, Women’s Aid, and Muslim counselling and Muslim women’s support services The Safety Center also carries emergency contact guidance. If you feel unsafe right now, call 911 first. Report to Muzz afterwards. How does Muzz protect your privacy? Photo privacy is standard on Muzz, not a paid upgrade. Members who prefer to keep their photos hidden for privacy or modesty can do that on the free tier. Muzz also offers free in-app voice and video calling, so you can see and speak to someone before meeting them without exchanging phone numbers. If you’d like to exchange phone numbers but we believe it is too early, we’ll actually nudge you by asking “Are you sure you want to share personal information?” One point of confusion worth clearing up: the Gold feature relating to blurred photos is a filter that lets paying members hide profiles whose photos are blurred. It does not change anyone’s ability to protect their own photos. Hiding yours is free. Why does Muzz limit you to five conversations? Muzz caps active conversations at five. Once you have five going, browsing pauses until you unmatch someone. You can have unlimited matches – the limit is on conversations, not connections. This has been documented in the Muzz help center since the feature launched, and the reason is straightforward: five real conversations that go somewhere are worth more than fifty that don’t. The limit applies to everyone, including Gold members. It isn’t a paywall and there is no version of Muzz you can buy that removes it. Muzz also prompts you when a conversation goes quiet from either side, to check whether you want to keep talking. What Muzz is doing about ghosting Relationship apps have a problem, and everyone using one already knows what it is. You send a message. Nothing. You send another. Seen, two weeks ago. Eventually you stop asking. Ghosting isn’t a safety issue in the way harassment or scams are. Nobody is in danger. But on an app built for marriage, being left hanging with no answer is its own kind of disrespect, and it is the single most common complaint we hear. So Muzz built accountability into the mechanic. If you have unanswered conversations, browsing stops until you deal with them – reply, or unmatch. Both are valid. Walking away is allowed. Disappearing while someone waits is not. Ending a conversation respectfully is a feature, not a failure. Not every match is the one, and saying so is kinder than silence. Is Muzz free, and what does Gold change? Matching and chatting on Muzz are free, and Muzz has committed to keeping them that way. You do not need to pay to meet someone or to talk to them. Gold adds: must-have filters so you only see matches within your preferences, more daily likes, a free weekly Profile Boost that puts you in front of around 30x more people, a filter to hide blurred-photo profiles, a hideable VIP badge, and Rematch after an unmatch. What Gold does not do: remove the five-conversation limit, unlock verification, or gate your own photo privacy. Safety features are not on the paid tier. How to stay safe on any Muslim marriage app This applies whether you use Muzz or not. Video call before you meet. The single most effective anti-catfish step there is, and it’s free on Muzz. Stay on the app early. Verification, moderation and reporting only work while you’re on the platform. Never send money. Not for an emergency, not for a flight, not for an investment. There is no version of this that ends well. Meet in public the first time (with a mahram). A café, a restaurant, somewhere with people. Bring someone if you want to. Tell someone where you’re going. A friend, a sibling, a parent — the person’s name, the place, the time. Guard your details. Home address, workplace, financial information — none of it belongs in an early conversation. Trust the feeling. If something is off, you don’t owe anyone an explanation. Unmatch, block, report. Frequently asked questions Is Muzz safe to use? Muzz requires mandatory selfie verification for every member, manually reviews profiles, and offers free blocking and reporting to all users. Photo privacy is available on the free tier. As with any app, your own precautions — video calling before meeting, staying on-platform early, never sending money — matter alongside the platform’s. Does Muzz verify its users? Yes. Every member must complete selfie verification, which compares a submitted selfie against the profile photo to confirm a real person is behind the account. The selfie is never shared with anyone and is used only for security. Verification is not a paid feature. Are there fake profiles on Muzz? Any large platform attracts bad actors. Muzz counters this with mandatory selfie verification, profile review, and an investigation process for impersonation reports. If you suspect someone is impersonating another person, report them. How do I block someone on Muzz? From their profile: scroll to the bottom, select Block, choose a reason, submit. From a chat: tap the three dots, then Block under Safety Options. They are not notified, and the block works both ways — they can’t see or message you, and you won’t see them either. What happens when you report someone on Muzz? Reports go to the moderation team for review, which can result in a ban. Muzz operates an appeals process so banned members can contest a decision. Why can’t I browse when I have five conversations? Muzz caps active conversations at five so members focus on real conversations rather than collecting matches. Reply or unmatch to free a slot. Matches are unlimited – only conversations are capped, and the limit applies to Gold members too. Does Muzz Gold remove the five-conversation limit? No. The limit applies to every member regardless of subscription. Gold adds filters, likes, Profile Boosts, Rematch and a VIP badge — it does not change conversation limits or unlock safety features. Is Muzz free? Yes. Matching and chatting are free and Muzz has committed to keeping them free. Gold is optional and adds visibility and convenience features. Still have a question? The Muzz help center covers profile setup, verification, safety and privacy, and the Safety Center holds the community guidelines and external support resources. If you feel unsafe right now, contact the police first.

title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From Kaiser Permanente
summary: Request Kaiser Permanente medical records in 2026 with verified authorization guidance, regional ROI contacts, timelines, and practical tips for law firms.
body_text: Kaiser Permanente is one of the largest integrated healthcare systems in the United States, and its regional structure can create additional complexity for personal injury attorneys retrieving medical records. Request procedures, contact routes, forms, and published processing estimates can differ by region, making it important to identify where a client received treatment before submitting a request. This guide covers Kaiser’s current authorization requirements, regional Release of Information contacts, submission procedures, and common issues legal teams should watch for. For firms that want to avoid managing these workflows manually, Codes Health combines medical record retrieval, authorization review, follow-up, completeness checks, and AI-powered medical record analysis for plaintiff law firms. Key Takeaways Kaiser’s current Kaiser authorization , NS-9934, is designed for third-party disclosures and includes “Legal” as a disclosure purpose. The form contains specific selections involving mental health treatment, addiction medicine treatment, and HIV lab results. Oregon locations also include a genetic-testing selection. Processing estimates vary by region and request type. Northern California currently tells patients to allow 5 business days, Georgia says up to 10 business days, and Hawaii says 10 to 15 business days for certain detailed electronic record requests. Southern California maintains multiple local Release of Information contacts through its records directory . Northwest Kaiser maintains centralized ROI contact information for Oregon and Southwest Washington. Codes Health reviews requests before submission and helps law firms manage medical record retrieval and identify potentially missing documentation through its legal use cases . Understanding the Kaiser Permanente Medical Records Request Process Kaiser’s regional structure matters because the applicable records workflow depends on where the patient received treatment. Northern California, Southern California, Georgia, Colorado, Hawaii, Washington, and the Northwest publish separate medical-record request pages and instructions. For legal teams, the safest process is to identify the treatment location first, confirm the appropriate Kaiser region, and then follow the current instructions published for that region. If treatment occurred across different Kaiser regions, confirm whether additional requests are necessary instead of assuming that one submission will automatically retrieve every relevant record. Processing Timelines Vary There is no single nationwide Kaiser turnaround time. Published estimates include: Northern California: Kaiser currently says to allow 5 business days for its online medical-record request process. Georgia: Kaiser says requests may take up to 10 business days. Hawaii: Kaiser says to allow 10 to 15 business days for detailed electronic records. These estimates relate to the specific workflows described on Kaiser’s regional pages and should not be treated as guaranteed attorney-request turnaround times. The completeness of the authorization, request scope, applicable fees, and regional procedures can affect the actual timeline. Codes Health focuses on reducing administrative delays by reviewing requests, following up with record custodians, and tracking retrieval through a purpose-built retrieval platform . Its company materials position standard retrieval in a couple of weeks rather than promising same-day service. Required Forms for Kaiser Permanente Medical Record Release Kaiser Permanente Authorization Form Kaiser’s current NS-9934 Authorization for Use or Disclosure of Patient Health Information, revision 08-21, is designed for disclosures to third parties. The same form identifies the Spanish version NS-1614 and the Chinese version NS-6274. Attorneys can review the current authorization form directly through Kaiser. The form should not be confused with every regional patient-access request form. Kaiser regions may provide separate workflows for patients requesting copies for themselves. Completing the Authorization The current NS-9934 asks for core patient identifying information, including the patient’s name, medical record number, birth date, and email address. It also requires information identifying the third-party recipient. For a law firm, recipient information should be complete and accurate so Kaiser knows where the requested material should be delivered. The form includes Legal among the available purposes for disclosure. Selecting the Records The current NS-9934 provides options covering categories such as: Form completion Medical records Diagnostic images Itemized billing records Pharmacy copays Medical copays The form also contains time-range selections for the material being authorized. Attorneys should review the actual Kaiser authorization rather than relying on older summaries of the form. Sensitive Records Kaiser’s authorization includes separate selections for certain categories of sensitive information, including: Mental Health Treatment Records Addiction Medicine Treatment Records HIV Lab Test Results Genetic Testing for Oregon locations Kaiser’s form warns that certain protected information will not be included if the applicable authorization selection is not made. For litigation teams, these selections can be important when the requested medical history involves behavioral health, substance-use treatment, HIV testing, or other specially protected information. The legal team should also consider applicable federal and state confidentiality laws before requesting or using sensitive records. Incomplete authorizations are a major source of avoidable record-request problems. Missing patient signatures, incomplete dates, unclear expiration information, and unchecked selections for relevant sensitive records can result in rejection or require a corrected submission. Codes Health reviews authorization information before submission and uses its medical retrieval workflow to flag issues that could delay a request. Kaiser Permanente Medical Records Contacts Kaiser Permanente Southern California Kaiser publishes a dedicated Southern California records page with local Release of Information contacts. Current local contacts include: Antelope Valley Phone: 661-726-2129 Email: avroiu@kp.org Baldwin Park Phone: 626-939-7120 Email: bpkroi@kp.org Downey Phone: 562-658-3140 Email: dnyroiu@kp.org Kern County Phone: 661-852-3450 Email: kernroiu@kp.org Los Angeles Phone: 213-580-6135 Email: laroiu@kp.org Orange County Phone: 714-284-6634 Email: ocroiu@kp.org Panorama City Phone: 818-375-2208 Email: pcroi@kp.org Riverside Phone: 951-353-4470 Email: rivroiu@kp.org San Bernardino County Phone: 909-609-3200 Email: fonroiu@kp.org San Diego Phone: 619-583-4293 Email: sdroiu@kp.org South Bay Phone: 310-517-2905 Email: sbroiu@kp.org West Los Angeles Phone: 323-857-2695 Email: wlaroi@kp.org Woodland Hills Phone: 818-719-2670 Email: whroiu@kp.org TTY: 711 Because Kaiser can update local contacts, legal teams should verify the destination on the official records directory before transmitting protected health information. Kaiser Permanente Northern California Northern California provides an online workflow where users can specify the date range, requested records, and receiving party. Kaiser currently tells users to allow 5 business days for completion through that workflow. The latest instructions are available through Northern California records . Northern California also allows patients to view frequently requested information online, including health summaries, test results, past-visit information, and visit histories. Kaiser Permanente Northwest Kaiser’s Northwest region covers Oregon and Southwest Washington. Its current Northwest records contact information includes: Email: nw.roi@kp.org Phone: 503-571-5051 Hours: 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday Toll-free: 800-813-2000 Mail: 500 NE Multnomah Street, Suite 100, Portland, OR 97232-2099 Kaiser instructs requesters to include the name, date of birth, and health record number of the person who received care in correspondence with the Northwest ROI department. Kaiser Permanente Georgia Current Georgia records instructions list the following general Medical Records Administration contact information: Email: release-of-information@kp.org Phone: 770-220-3870 Fax: 770-220-3705 Mail: Kaiser Permanente Georgia, Medical Records Administration, 3200 Breckinridge Blvd., Duluth, GA 30096 Kaiser states that these requests may take up to 10 business days. Some requests are subject to fees, and where a fee applies Kaiser states that payment is required before the records are released. The Georgia page also contains separate contact numbers for certain requests involving another person. Because Kaiser publishes more than one routing pathway on the same page, attorneys should confirm the appropriate submission route before transmitting records or authorizations. Kaiser Permanente Colorado Kaiser’s current Colorado records instructions provide these Release of Information contacts: Phone: 303-404-4700 Email: KPCOReleaseofInfo@kp.org Fax: 303-404-4750 Mail: Northfield Support Services, Attn: Release of Information, 11000 E. 45th Avenue, Denver, CO 80239-3004 Kaiser allows the authorization to be submitted electronically, by email, by fax, or by mail using the procedures described on its regional page. Kaiser Permanente Hawaii Kaiser Hawaii currently tells patients to allow 10 to 15 business days for completion of a detailed electronic medical-record request. Its Hawaii records page lists: Phone: 808-432-5092 Fax: 866-609-7402 Email: HI-ROI@kp.org The Hawaii online health summary contains commonly requested information, but Kaiser describes it as a summary rather than a complete medical record. Kaiser Permanente Washington Washington uses a separate authorization and regional routing structure. The current Washington records page lists the following contacts. Western Washington Mail: Kaiser Foundation Health Plan of Washington, Release of Information, RCR-A3E-01, P.O. Box 9010, Renton, WA 98057-9010 Phone: 1-866-656-4184 Fax: 877-848-6896 Email: kpwa-roi@kp.org Eastern Washington Mail: Kaiser Foundation Health Plan of Washington, Release of Information, RFM-W200C2, P.O. Box 204, Spokane, WA 99210-0204 Phone: 509-241-7824 Fax: 855-414-1751 Email: kpwa-roi@kp.org Kaiser directs Washington residents treated in the Vancouver or Longview area to the Northwest records process instead. Accessing Kaiser Permanente Medical Records Online Patients can access portions of their health information through Kaiser’s online tools. Depending on the region, online information may include: Health summaries Test results Visit summaries Medication information Immunizations Current health conditions For example, Northern California allows users to view health summaries, test results, past visits, and complete visit histories, while Hawaii explains that its downloadable health summary contains many common health-record elements but is still only a summary. For law firms, patient portal material may be useful for initial case evaluation, but a portal download should not automatically be treated as the complete litigation record. Cases may require formal retrieval of detailed medical records, billing records, diagnostic imaging, or documents that are not immediately available through the patient-facing portal. Requesting Kaiser Records for a Law Firm Complete the Authorization For a third-party recipient such as an attorney or law firm, the current Kaiser authorization should be reviewed carefully. Important fields include: Patient identifying information Third-party recipient information Purpose of disclosure Requested record categories Applicable date range Sensitive-information selections Patient signature and date Do not automatically assume that every Kaiser region requires a copy of the patient’s government-issued ID with an attorney request. The current NS-9934 itself does not establish a universal photo-ID attachment requirement. Specific situations, such as in-person pickup of Washington imaging records, can have separate identification rules. Use Current Routing The appropriate submission method varies by region. Georgia accepts paperwork by email, fax, or mail. Colorado publishes electronic, email, fax, and mail options. Washington publishes separate Western and Eastern Washington routes. Because these procedures can change, firms should check the relevant Kaiser page before each submission rather than relying indefinitely on stored fax numbers or addresses. Integrating Retrieval Workflows For firms using Filevine, the Filevine integration from Codes Health is designed to connect medical record retrieval with the firm’s case-management workflow. Codes Health states that Filevine users can manage retrieval-related work from within their existing case environment. For high-volume legal customers, Codes Health can also support custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical or case-management software. Its engineering team continues to develop additional workflows and products as the platform expands. Ensuring Completeness of Kaiser Permanente Records Review Sensitive Authorizations If sensitive records are relevant to the case, check whether the appropriate selections were completed before submission. Kaiser’s NS-9934 contains specific authorization choices involving mental health, addiction treatment, and HIV information. Verify the Region Confirm where treatment occurred and use the correct Kaiser regional process. Washington, for example, directs patients treated around Vancouver and Longview to the Northwest regional records process. Check Patient Information Confirm that names, dates of birth, medical record numbers when available, dates of service, and recipient information are accurate before submitting the request. Incomplete authorizations are a leading avoidable cause of denied or delayed medical record requests. Missing signatures, unclear expiration information, unchecked sensitive-record selections, and patient-information errors can require correction before a provider will complete a request. Codes Health uses AI-supported request review to flag problems such as misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues before submission. Its retrieval resources also focus on workflows used by plaintiff law firms. Review Every Production When records arrive, the legal team should compare the production against the original request: Confirm requested dates are represented Verify requested record types are present Check for chronological gaps Look for unreadable pages Review whether billing and treatment records align Identify referenced records that appear to be absent Codes Health’s platform is designed to flag gaps and potentially missing documentation so law firms can identify incomplete productions earlier in case preparation. Older or Archived Kaiser Permanente Records Medical-record retention requirements vary by state, facility type, record type, and patient circumstances. Attorneys should not assume that every Kaiser region follows the same nationwide retention period. For older records: Identify the Kaiser region and treatment facility. Provide the most precise treatment dates available. Include the patient’s identifying information. Ask the applicable ROI office whether archived records remain available. Expect older or archived material to potentially require additional processing. Using the applicable regional Kaiser records page is preferable to relying on an old facility address or an outdated request form. HIPAA and Patient Access Rights The HIPAA Privacy Rule generally gives individuals the right to inspect and obtain copies of medical and billing records held by covered healthcare providers and health plans, subject to limited exceptions. HHS provides an overview of these HIPAA access rights . For an individual exercising the HIPAA right of access, a provider may charge only certain reasonable, cost-based fees permitted by the Privacy Rule. HHS explains that covered entities cannot include search and retrieval costs in the individual’s access fee. The agency provides additional HIPAA fee guidance . These HIPAA patient-access rules should not automatically be applied to every attorney, subpoena, or litigation request. The applicable legal framework can depend on who is requesting the information, the form of authorization, state law, and whether compulsory legal process is involved. Who Can Act for a Patient? HIPAA recognizes circumstances in which a legally authorized personal representative can exercise rights on behalf of an individual. HHS explains that the scope of access can depend on the representative’s legal authority. Kaiser or applicable law may require supporting documents in situations involving: Legal guardians Personal representatives Powers of attorney Deceased patients Minor patients Law firms should confirm the documentation needed for the specific patient and jurisdiction instead of assuming one representative document works nationwide. Efficient Kaiser Retrieval with Codes Health For plaintiff firms, the burden of Kaiser record retrieval goes beyond sending an authorization. Staff may need to identify the correct region, confirm the appropriate destination, correct authorization issues, monitor outstanding requests, reconcile incomplete productions, and pursue missing records. Codes Health brings retrieval, tracking, medical-record organization, and AI-supported review into one platform built for plaintiff law firms. AI-Validated Requests Authorization problems can delay record retrieval. Code Health reviews requests before submission and can identify potential issues involving: Patient-information misspellings Missing dates of service Signature problems Authorization gaps Potentially missing records For sensitive-record requests, missing patient signatures, unclear expiration information, or unchecked authorization selections can require corrected paperwork. Codes Health’s review workflow is intended to catch these problems before they create additional provider back-and-forth. Purpose-Built Medical AI General-purpose AI platforms, including ChatGPT and similar tools, are not substitutes for purpose-built medical record analysis when a law firm needs a consistent, source-grounded review of complex clinical documents. Codes Health combines specialized medical-record workflows with AI analysis designed for plaintiff-side legal cases, including tools for identifying missing records and organizing case-relevant medical information. The platform continues to expand through an MIT-educated engineering team that builds additional workflows, integrations, and products for medical-record retrieval and review. High-Volume Integrations Legal teams managing significant request volume can use Codes Health alongside existing case-management workflows, including its current Filevine integration . Custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical or legal software can also help high-volume customers reduce manual data entry and keep retrieval activity connected to their existing case workflows. Frequently Asked Questions How long does it take to get medical records from Kaiser Permanente? Processing times vary by Kaiser region and request type. Northern California currently tells users to allow 5 business days for its online medical-record request, Georgia says requests may take up to 10 business days, and Hawaii says detailed electronic medical-record requests may take 10 to 15 business days. These are regional processing estimates rather than guarantees for every attorney request, so firms should confirm current instructions through the appropriate Kaiser records page before submitting a request. Is there a fee for Kaiser medical records? Fees depend on the region, request type, and legal basis for the request. Georgia, for example, states that some requests are subject to a fee and that payment is required before release when a fee applies. For individuals exercising their HIPAA access rights, federal regulations generally limit providers to specified reasonable, cost-based charges and do not allow search and retrieval costs to be included. HHS explains the applicable rules in its fee guidance . What should I do if Kaiser records appear incomplete? Compare the production with the original request, including the date ranges, requested record types, billing records, imaging, and any sensitive-information selections. Look for treatment referenced in one document that does not appear elsewhere in the production, and contact the correct Kaiser ROI office when specific material appears to be missing. Codes Health can help legal teams identify gaps through its medical retrieval and record-review workflows. Can Kaiser send records directly to an attorney? Yes. Kaiser’s NS-9934 is designed for disclosure to a third-party recipient and includes “Legal” as an available purpose of disclosure. The patient should accurately identify the recipient, the records being authorized, the applicable sensitive-information selections, and other required information before signing the current authorization form . How can firms reduce Kaiser retrieval delays? Start by identifying the correct Kaiser region, using the current authorization form, verifying patient and recipient information, selecting all legally appropriate record categories, and checking the production for gaps as soon as it arrives. For firms that do not want staff manually managing those steps, Codes Health provides medical record retrieval, tracking, completeness review, and AI-supported analysis in a platform designed for plaintiff law firms.

title: MaxLinear Expands AI Infrastructure Control-Plane Portfolio with Intelligent eFuse Solutions for Rack-Scale Power Protection and Telemetry
body_text: MaxLinear Expands AI Infrastructure Control-Plane Portfolio with Intelligent eFuse Solutions for Rack-Scale Power Protection and Telemetry Download as PDF August 10, 2026 New MxL745950 and MxL745951P address growing hyperscaler demand for intelligent power protection and telemetry solutions and will be showcased at the OCP APAC 2026 Summit booth PL33 CARLSBAD, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- MaxLinear, Inc. (NASDAQ: MXL), a leader in high-performance analog, mixed-signal and connectivity semiconductor solutions, today announced the expansion of its AI infrastructure portfolio with two new 16V high-current electronic fuse (eFuse) solutions, the MxL745950 and MxL745951P. AI infrastructure is driving unprecedented increases in rack power density, power-domain complexity, and serviceability requirements. The devices are designed to help hyperscalers, OEMs, ODMs, and networking equipment providers protect, monitor, and manage critical power paths across AI servers, accelerator trays, data center switches, fan trays, power shelves, plug-in modules, and rack-scale platforms. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260810522477/en/ MaxLinear's MxL745950 and MxL745951P intelligent eFuse solutions help enable scalable power protection, telemetry, and fault isolation for next-generation AI infrastructure. As AI clusters scale from server-centric deployments to rack-scale systems, power-path protection is becoming a mission-critical element of platform reliability. MaxLinear’s new eFuse portfolio brings together integrated hot-swap protection, scalable high-current operation, compact implementation, and intelligent monitoring to help customers improve uptime, isolate faults, accelerate root-cause analysis, and gain deeper visibility into power-domain behavior across large-scale AI deployments. Industry demand for AI infrastructure continues to accelerate. Market research estimates that data center semiconductor revenue will reach approximately $843 billion by 2030. Hyperscaler capital spending is also rising sharply as operators expand AI compute capacity to support training, inference, and emerging agentic workloads. These trends are increasing the need for highly reliable power protection, telemetry, and serviceability across servers, networking systems, accelerator platforms, and rack-level infrastructure. Industry estimates place the global eFuse market at approximately $1.0B today, with growth expected through 2030 as electronic systems require more intelligent, compact, resettable, and programmable power protection. When viewed together with adjacent hot-swap and intelligent power-path protection ICs used in data center, telecom, automotive, and industrial infrastructure, the broader opportunity expands into a multi-billion-dollar power-protection market. The MxL745950 is a 16V, 50A electronic fuse with 1mΩ on-resistance in a compact 5mm × 5mm LGA-32 package. It integrates current sensing, temperature monitoring, fault indication, programmable soft-start and parallel-operation capability for higher-current applications, such as servers, networking systems, and plug-in modules. The MxL745951P is a 16V, 60A stackable eFuse with 0.79mΩ on-resistance, PMBus™/I²C interface support, high-precision telemetry, configurable protection thresholds, non-volatile fault recording, and active current balancing during start-up and steady-state operation. The device provides digital telemetry for input voltage, input current, input energy, output voltage, output current, input power, and output power, enabling platform designers to add more intelligent power monitoring and fault visibility in AI and high-performance computing infrastructure. “As AI infrastructure scales, the opportunity is expanding beyond compute silicon into the control, power, and telemetry technologies required to operate dense racks reliably,” said Amit D. Bavisi, Ph.D., Senior Vice President and General Manager, Analog Mixed-Signal Business Unit at MaxLinear. “Our new eFuse solutions extend MaxLinear’s role across AI servers, accelerator trays, switches, fan trays, power shelves, and rack-level platforms by helping customers build more observable, serviceable, and resilient power architectures.” Why AI Infrastructure Requires Intelligent Power Protection Rack-level fault isolation: Integrated protection and fault-management capabilities help isolate subsystem failures before they impact broader rack operation. Operational visibility: High-precision telemetry and fault recording help operators improve power-domain visibility and accelerate root-cause analysis. Scalable current handling: Parallel operation and active current balancing support increasingly dense AI platforms and higher-current accelerator deployments. Serviceability and uptime: Hot-swap and inrush-control capabilities help support maintenance and replacement workflows in live or service-sensitive infrastructure. Control-plane integration: Complements MaxLinear’s AI infrastructure portfolio spanning connectivity, monitoring, rack management, console access, telemetry, power management, and protection. Optimized for AI Data Center Power Protection High-current capability: Up to 50A for MxL745950 and up to 60A for MxL745951P per device, with parallel operation support for higher-current applications. Low-loss integrated power path: Integrated MOSFETs with low on-resistance help reduce power loss and voltage droop in dense systems. Hot-swap and inrush control: Programmable or configurable soft-start helps limit inrush current during card insertion and backplane hot-plug events. Robust protection: Integrated UVP, OVP, OCP, SCP, OTP, MOSFET fault diagnosis, and fault reporting improve system protection and status visibility. Advanced telemetry and configurability: MxL745951P adds PMBus/I²C telemetry, configurable thresholds and timers, black-box fault recording, and NVM-based custom configuration storage. Compact footprint: 5mm × 5mm LGA-32 and 5mm × 4.5mm VQFN-26L packages support space-constrained board designs. Product Summary Product Positioning Key Specifications Monitoring / interface Package MxL745950 16V/50A eFuse for servers, networking, plug-in modules, and compact power-path protection 4V to 16V input; up to 50A; 1mΩ RDS(ON) Analog current sensing, temperature monitoring, fault indication 5mm × 5mm LGA-32 MxL745951P 16V/60A stackable eFuse for server/HPC, data center switches/routers, accelerator trays, and fan trays 2.9V to 16V input; up to 60A; 0.79mΩ RDS(ON) PMBus/I²C telemetry, ±1% current monitoring accuracy, black-box fault recording, NVM configuration 5mm × 4.5mm VQFN-26L OCP APAC 2026 Demonstration and Availability MaxLinear will introduce its new eFuse portfolio at the 2026 OCP APAC Summit, taking place August 11-12, 2026 at TaiNEX2 in Taipei City, Taiwan. The MxL745950 and MxL745951P will be showcased at Booth PL33, alongside MaxLinear’s broader AI infrastructure portfolio for rack-scale management, connectivity, telemetry, power management, and protection. Customer meetings will be held in Meeting Room 4. The MxL745950 and MxL745951P are sampling now with volume production expected in Q4 2026. Visit maxlinear.com/mxl745950 and maxlinear.com/mxl745951P for more information. Customers interested in evaluating the new eFuse solutions can contact MaxLinear for additional product information and availability details. title: Sypris Reports Second Quarter Results

body_text: PDF Version Satellite and Deep Space Programs Drive 25% Increase in Orders LOUISVILLE, Ky.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 18, 2026-- Sypris Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq/GM: SYPR) today reported financial results for its second quarter ended July 5, 2026. HIGHLIGHTS Orders increased 25% sequentially for the Company, driven by a 54% increase in bookings at Sypris Electronics for satellite and deep space programs, and subsea fiber-optic data network systems. Orders for energy products remained strong during the period, resulting in a 12% increase in bookings for the first half of 2026 when compared to the prior-year period. Revenue for Sypris Technologies increased 5.6% year over year and 19.9% sequentially, driven by the resurgent expansion of the commercial vehicle market and strong energy product sales. Gross profit for Sypris Technologies increased 28% year over year and 94% sequentially, reflecting an improvement in margins of 330 and 710 basis points, respectively. Revenue for Sypris Electronics increased 15.4% sequentially, with the outlook for the balance of the year poised for substantial additional growth driven by robust orders and improved material availability. “The escalation of geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East has accelerated demand for inventory replenishment and critical technology upgrades, thereby placing a premium on rapid, efficient scaling,” commented Jeffrey T. Gill, President and Chief Executive Officer. “Sypris Electronics, with its advanced production capabilities, deep technical expertise and strong market position, is uniquely equipped to capitalize on these dynamics. While material availability and a series of temporary operational headwinds impacted our performance during the first half of 2026, we are actively resolving these challenges to unlock our full earnings potential going forward. “Orders for our energy products increased 12% year over year in the first half of 2026, with strong backlog and expected orders on several large projects. Additional growth opportunities may emerge from new global initiatives addressing rising LNG demand and the massive surge in electricity required by AI-related data centers. Furthermore, we are actively pursuing applications for our products in adjacent markets including carbon capture and defense applications to further diversify our industry and customer portfolios. “As we cross the midpoint of 2026, the North American commercial vehicle market has transitioned into what may prove to be an extended expansion cycle, reflecting increasing fleet profitability, accelerating freight rates and rising infrastructure demand.” Second Quarter Results The Company reported revenue of $30.3 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to $31.4 million for the prior-year comparable period. Additionally, the Company reported a net loss of $3.1 million, or $0.14 per share, compared with a net loss of $2.1 million, or $0.09 per share, for the prior-year period. Results for the second quarter of 2026 included $2.1 million in abnormally high expenses for healthcare, unabsorbed overhead, foreign exchange variances, charges for scrap and accruals for excess and obsolete inventory as compared to the prior-year period. For the six months ended July 5, 2026, the Company reported revenue of $56.2 million compared to $60.9 million for the first half of 2025. The Company reported a net loss of $7.2 million compared with a net loss of $3.0 million for the prior-year period. Results for the six months ended July 5, 2026, included $4.5 million in increased expenses for healthcare, unabsorbed overhead, foreign exchange variances, charges for scrap and accruals for excess and obsolete inventory as compared to the prior-year period. Sypris Technologies Revenue for Sypris Technologies was $14.9 million in the second quarter of 2026 compared to $14.1 million for the prior-year period, reflecting strong energy product sales. Additionally, the commercial vehicle market began to rebound during the second quarter from the cyclical decline experienced over the prior year. Gross profit for the second quarter of 2026 was $2.7 million, or 18.5% of revenue, compared to $2.1 million, or 15.2% of revenue, for the same period in 2025. Gross profit for the second quarter of 2026 was positively impacted by the increase in volumes, partially offset by a $0.5 million unfavorable impact from foreign currency exchange rates for our Mexican subsidiary. Sypris Electronics Revenue for Sypris Electronics was $15.5 million in the second quarter of 2026 compared to $17.3 million for the prior-year period as a result of material availability issues in addition to customer design changes on certain new programs, which pushed out delivery dates. Gross profit for the second quarter of 2026 was a loss of $0.8 million, or (4.9%) of revenue, compared to $0.4 million, or 2.5% of revenue, for the same period in 2025. Material availability issues have delayed certain customer deliveries, limited our ability to ramp up production in response to customer demand for certain products and have caused out-of-sequence manufacturing, which increases costs and decreases operational efficiency. Additionally, gross profit for the second quarter of 2026 reflected the impact of $0.7 million of charges for excess and obsolete inventory taken during the period. Outlook Commenting on the future, Mr. Gill added, “We expect the challenging operating environment to improve as we move through 2026. Backed by our robust backlog and recent program wins, we are optimistic that the balance of the year will reflect both accelerating top line growth and vastly improved operational performance.” About Sypris Solutions Sypris Solutions provides products and engineering, design, and manufacturing services for a variety of critical infrastructure sectors, including energy, space, communications, defense, transport, chemical, and water. Sypris serves its customers globally through its operations located in North America. For more information about the Company, please visit its website at www.sypris.com . Forward Looking Statements This press release contains “forward-looking” statements within the meaning of the federal securities laws. Forward-looking statements include our plans and expectations of future financial and operational performance. Each forward-looking statement herein is subject to risks and uncertainties, as detailed in our most recent Form 10-K and Form 10-Q and other SEC filings. our failure to achieve and maintain profitability on a timely basis by steadily increasing our revenues from profitable contracts with a diversified group of customers, which would cause us to continue to use existing cash resources or require us to sell assets to fund operating losses; volatility of our customers’ forecasts and our contractual obligations to meet current scheduling demands and production levels, which may negatively impact our operational capacity and our effectiveness to integrate new customers or suppliers, and in turn cause increases in our inventory and working capital levels; title: Instrument serverless apps with agentic onboarding
summary: Use Datadog agentic onboarding to instrument AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Run, and Azure Container Apps from an AI assistant or CLI.
body_text: Rohan Agarwal PM intern Serverless platforms like AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Run, and Azure Container Apps let teams run applications without managing infrastructure. However, getting full visibility into those workloads has traditionally required a lot of manual setup. A single team may deploy serverless applications across multiple clouds by using tools such as Terraform, AWS SAM, AWS CDK, and the Serverless Framework. Each of these platforms, runtimes, and deployment tools requires its own instrumentation steps. Datadog’s serverless agentic onboarding simplifies serverless instrumentation by adapting setup to your existing deployment tools, runtimes, and serverless platforms. You can instrument serverless applications by describing what you want in plain language to an AI assistant connected to the Datadog MCP Server , or by running a single AI Setup CLI command. The onboarding flow generates the appropriate configuration for your unique environment and prepares changes for review before they’re applied. In this post, we’ll explain how you can use serverless agentic onboarding to: Instrument serverless applications from an AI assistant or CLI Adapt instrumentation to your existing serverless stack Review changes with built-in safety guardrails Instrument serverless applications from an AI assistant or CLI Serverless agentic onboarding provides two ways to instrument your serverless applications for Datadog without requiring you to manually identify every platform-specific step. Both options inspect your project, determine which setup instructions apply, and prepare changes within your local development environment. Datadog MCP Server The Datadog MCP Server connects an MCP-compatible coding assistant, such as Claude Code or Cursor, to Datadog. You can start the workflow with a prompt such as “Add Datadog for AWS Lambda to my project.” With your permission, the assistant examines the project, calls the relevant Datadog onboarding tools, and prepares the required configuration changes. AI Setup CLI The AI Setup CLI provides the same type of guided setup from your terminal without requiring an MCP-compatible assistant. You can run the CLI in your project directory by using Node.js 22 or later: npx @datadog/ai-setup-cli --product serverless The CLI can identify the files that define your application and infrastructure, ask for the information it needs, and prepare instrumentation changes in place. This approach is useful when you prefer a command-line workflow or do not want to connect an MCP server to your coding assistant. Adapt instrumentation to your existing serverless stack Serverless instrumentation differs across cloud platforms, deployment tools, and runtimes. Agentic onboarding detects the technologies already present and generates a configuration in the format that the project uses. For AWS Lambda, agentic onboarding supports projects deployed by using AWS SAM, the AWS CDK, the Serverless Framework, Terraform, or datadog-ci . Depending on the project, it can configure the Datadog Lambda library and Datadog Lambda Extension for supported Node.js, Python, Java, .NET, Ruby, and Go applications. For Google Cloud Run, the onboarding flow can instrument Cloud Run services and Cloud Run functions. It prepares a Terraform configuration that runs the Datadog Agent as a sidecar or includes the Agent within the application container by updating a Dockerfile. For Azure Container Apps, agentic onboarding supports both sidecar and in-container instrumentation. The sidecar approach uses Terraform, while the in-container approach updates a Dockerfile. In each case, the generated changes follow the structure of the existing project rather than requiring you to translate generic setup instructions into the appropriate configuration files. Agentic onboarding also configures the environment variables and reserved service, env, and version tags that apply to the selected workload. This helps teams use consistent tagging across serverless applications even when those applications run on different clouds or use different deployment frameworks. Review changes with built-in safety guardrails Because agentic onboarding writes real deployment and application changes, the flow includes guardrails that help keep its output predictable, reviewable, and under your control: Scope the setup before writing code: For Azure Container Apps and Google Cloud Run, the assistant asks a defined set of questions about your workload and the Datadog capabilities you want to configure. AWS Lambda uses a different flow based on its supported deployment tools and runtime-specific instrumentation options. Apply changes safely within your local workflow: Agentic onboarding applies and stages changes locally so that you can inspect the diff, test the configuration, or open a pull request. Nothing is committed on your behalf, and an AI coding assistant requests permission before modifying project files. Apply Datadog-recommended configuration: Each setup uses the appropriate Agent version; reserved service , env , and version tags; and environment variables for your runtime and selected telemetry. Maintain control over deployment: You can review, approve, and deploy the generated changes while reducing the manual work required to instrument serverless applications. Together, these guardrails help reduce the risk of applying a configuration that does not match your environment. They also keep your existing review, testing, approval, and deployment controls in place while reducing the manual work required to instrument serverless applications. Instrument serverless workloads with less manual setup Agentic onboarding for serverless reduces the manual work required to instrument serverless applications across clouds, runtimes, and deployment tools while keeping configuration changes reviewable. To configure the Datadog MCP Server or AI Setup CLI, see the serverless agentic onboarding documentation . For more information about collecting metrics, traces, and logs from serverless workloads, read the Serverless Monitoring documentation . If you don’t have a Datadog account, sign up for a 14-day free trial .

title: Warm Transfer vs. Cold Transfer: What Customers Actually Prefer
summary: {{IdKoVP5R3}}
body_text: Understanding the mechanics of each transfer type clarifies both why cold transfers became the default and why warm transfers, despite their clear customer preference advantages, have historically been harder to scale. The Mechanics of a Cold Transfer A cold transfer is operationally simple. The agent receives an inbound call, determines it needs to go elsewhere, and uses their phone system or softphone to blind-transfer the caller to another extension, queue, or number. No conversation with the receiving agent. No context packet. No introduction. The caller lands in the new destination and the original agent's line is freed immediately. From a pure efficiency standpoint, cold transfers are fast for the agent making them. That is their primary appeal inside a contact center under volume pressure. When handle time is a key metric and agents are measured on calls-per-hour, a cold transfer is a 10-second action. A warm transfer might take two to four minutes longer per call. The problem, as discussed, is that the time saved by the transferring agent is largely displaced onto the receiving agent and the caller. The receiving agent spends the first several minutes of the interaction extracting information that the caller has already provided. The caller loses patience, sometimes drops the call, and the resolution rate for that interaction falls. In aggregate, contact centers that rely heavily on cold transfers tend to see higher repeat contact rates. Customers who did not get resolution on a transfer call back, which costs more overall than the time that was nominally saved on the original transfer. The Mechanics of a Warm Transfer A warm transfer adds a deliberate handoff step. When the first agent determines a transfer is needed, they put the caller on hold briefly, dial or conference the receiving agent, provide a verbal briefing (name, situation, intent, urgency), and then conference the caller in and formally introduce them to the new agent. The original agent then exits the call. Some contact centers use a supervised transfer variant where the original agent stays on briefly after the introduction to confirm the receiving agent has what they need before dropping. This is common in high-stakes contexts like wealth management calls or complex insurance claims. The additional steps require training, time, and a contact center culture that prioritizes resolution quality over raw handle-time speed. This has historically made warm transfers feel like a premium option that only certain teams or certain call types get. Why Cold Transfers Became the Default (And Why That Is Changing) For most of the history of call centers, warm transfers were constrained by the limits of human agent capacity. If an agent was already handling a high-volume queue, asking them to take a warm transfer briefing before every handoff was genuinely difficult to staff for. Three things are changing this calculus now. First, CRM integration has improved. Modern platforms like Salesforce and HubSpot can push caller context to a receiving agent's screen the moment a transfer is initiated. This means even a brief warm verbal handoff can be supplemented by a full data packet, reducing the briefing time without sacrificing context quality. Second, AI voice agents are replacing the first leg of many calls. When an AI agent handles the initial intake, it is not working against a handle-time metric. It can spend as long as needed gathering and confirming caller context before routing. And because the AI system is integrated with the CRM and knowledge base, the context it collects can be passed to the receiving human agent in real time, with full fidelity, at the moment of transfer. Third, customer expectations have shifted upward. The companies that get customer experience right (in banking, in digital health, in direct-to-consumer insurance) have reset what callers consider acceptable. Being asked to repeat yourself in 2025 feels more jarring than it did in 2015. How AI Voice Agents Are Automating the Warm Handoff This is where AI voice agents and platforms like Feather AI are rewriting the operational logic of call transfers. In a traditional human-only contact center, a warm transfer is a manual process bounded by agent time and attention. An AI-first contact center changes the model fundamentally. Here is how a modern warm transfer works when the first leg is an AI voice agent: The AI agent answers the inbound call immediately, no queue wait. It identifies the caller, verifies identity if required, and gathers context through a natural conversation (not a scripted menu). When the AI determines the caller needs a human specialist, it does not just dump the call. It initiates a warm transfer with full context: caller name, account information, the nature of the inquiry, what the caller has already confirmed, and a suggested next action for the human agent. The human agent receives the call with a real-time context summary. They already know who they are talking to and why. The caller's experience is seamless. They feel like the organization actually listened to them during the first part of the call. This is not a theoretical future state. It is a capability that production AI voice platforms are delivering today. And it makes the warm transfer the default , not the exception, because the AI is not constrained by handle-time pressure the way a human agent is. Comparing Approaches: AI Warm Transfer vs. Human Warm Transfer vs. Cold Transfer Approach Context Continuity Caller Experience Operational Cost Cold transfer (human) None Lowest rated Lowest per-transfer Warm transfer (human only) High (verbal) Highest rated Highest per-transfer AI intake + warm transfer Very high (verbal + data push) Highest rated Lower at scale The AI-assisted warm transfer is not just a customer experience upgrade. It is an operational efficiency play. The AI handles the intake and context-gathering at a fraction of the cost of a human agent doing the same work, and the warm handoff it produces is often more complete than what a rushed human agent would provide under volume pressure. Named Competitor Context: How Different Platforms Handle Warm Transfer Not all AI voice platforms treat warm transfer as a core capability. It is worth being specific about how the landscape looks. Vapi is a developer-first voice infrastructure platform. It is highly flexible and technically capable, but warm transfer is something your engineering team configures from scratch. If you have the in-house dev resources, you can build it. If you do not, it is not ready out of the box. Retell AI sits in a middle position, offering more business-user tooling than Vapi but still requiring meaningful technical setup for production-grade warm transfer workflows. Bland AI is built primarily for high-volume outbound calling. Warm transfer capability, along with appointment scheduling and SMS follow-up, is gated behind their Enterprise tier, which means growing teams may not have access to it without a larger commitment. Feather AI ships warm transfer with full context push as a standard capability, not a premium add-on. The integration with Salesforce and HubSpot means the context packet that accompanies the warm transfer includes live CRM data, not just what the AI gathered in the current call. This is particularly relevant for financial services, healthcare, and insurance teams where account history is part of every conversation.

title: Boise Cascade reports second quarterly 2026 results
summary: BOISE, IDAHO — August 3, 2026 — Boise Cascade Company (“Boise Cascade,” the “Company,” “we,” or “our”) (NYSE: BCC) today reported net income of $57.3 million, or $1.63 per share, on sales of $1.8 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared with net income of $62.0 million, or $1.64 per share, on […]
body_text: BOISE, IDAHO — August 3, 2026 — Boise Cascade Company (“Boise Cascade,” the “Company,” “we,” or “our”) (NYSE: BCC) today reported net income of $57.3 million, or $1.63 per share, on sales of $1.8 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared with net income of $62.0 million, or $1.64 per share, on sales of $1.7 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2025. Second quarter 2025 results included $5.8 million of after-tax gains, or $0.15 per share, on the sale of non-operating properties. “I am excited to announce an outstanding second quarter, in what continues to be a mixed demand backdrop. These results reflect the power of our people and the service capabilities that our integrated model delivers to the marketplace,” said Jeff Strom, CEO. “By combining nationwide scale with strong local support, we delivered the reliable service and consistent value our customers have come to expect from us across a broad mix of industry-leading building materials. The recent announcement of our expanded partnership with James Hardie to become the sole nationwide distributor of their full portfolio of industry-leading exterior and outdoor building products further strengthens our ability to distinguish ourselves in the marketplace. Looking ahead, we will continue to advance strategic priorities that position us to grow share, drive efficiencies, and return capital to shareholders while supporting our customers’ and suppliers’ success.” Read the full news release for more information. Investor Contact: Chris Forrey, [email protected] Media Contact: Amy Evans, [email protected] About Boise Cascade Boise Cascade is one of the largest U.S. wholesale distributors of building materials and a leading manufacturer of engineered wood products and plywood in North America. Our integrated model and national distribution footprint position us to deliver outstanding service to our customers across a broad range of industry-leading products, including key structural products that we produce. Headquartered in Boise, Idaho, we operate more than 60 distribution and manufacturing facilities strategically located across the U.S. and Canada. Our work is powered by a dedicated team of over 7,500 people. For more information, visit: Boise Cascade | Our Company . Webcast and Conference Call Boise Cascade will host a webcast and conference call to discuss second quarter earnings on Tuesday, August 4, 2026, at 11 a.m. Eastern. To join the webcast, go to the Investors section of this website and select the Event Calendar link. Analysts and investors who wish to ask questions during the Q&A session can register for the call here. The archived webcast will be available in the Investors section of this website. Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures We refer to the terms EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA in this earnings release and the accompanying Quarterly Statistical Information as supplemental measures of our performance and liquidity that are not required by or presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (GAAP). We define EBITDA as income before interest (interest expense and interest income), income taxes, and depreciation and amortization. Additionally, we disclose Adjusted EBITDA, which further adjusts EBITDA to exclude the change in fair value of interest rate swaps. We also disclose Segment EBITDA, which is segment income (loss) before depreciation and amortization. We believe EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA are meaningful measures because they present a transparent view of our recurring operating performance and allow management to readily view operating trends, perform analytical comparisons, and identify strategies to improve operating performance. We also believe EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA are useful to investors because they provide a means to evaluate the operating performance of our segments and our Company on an ongoing basis using criteria that are used by our management and because they are frequently used by investors and other interested parties when comparing companies in our industry that have different financing and capital structures and/or tax rates. EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA, however, are not measures of our liquidity or financial performance under GAAP and should not be considered as alternatives to net income, income from operations, or any other performance measure derived in accordance with GAAP or as alternatives to cash flow from operating activities as a measure of our liquidity. The use of EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA instead of net income or segment income (loss) have limitations as analytical tools, including: the inability to determine profitability; the exclusion of interest expense, interest income, and associated significant cash requirements; and the exclusion of depreciation and amortization, which represent unavoidable operating costs. Management compensates for these limitations by relying on our GAAP results. Our measures of EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA are not necessarily comparable to other similarly titled captions of other companies due to potential inconsistencies in the methods of calculation. For a reconciliation of net income to EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA and segment income to Segment EBITDA, please see the section titled, “Summary Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements and Segment Information” below. title: Tesorio Named to the Inc. 5000 for the Fourth Consecutive Year
body_text: Tesorio is on the Inc. 5000 again this week. Four years in a row now. We build software for finance teams, so before we celebrate a number, habit says to ask what it actually measures. A ranking is a lagging indicator. It tells you something already happened. The interesting question is what. Here is what one appearance measures: revenue growth across a trailing three-year window. For the 2026 list, that means 2025 revenue against 2022. Clearing that bar even once is a real achievement, and it can be done in a sprint: a hot category, a big launch, one great year of sales. Four consecutive appearances stretch that measurement across seven years of the business. And the story goes back further still. Tesorio has been building for finance teams since 2015, more than a decade now. Those seven years were not one market. They covered the zero-interest era, the end of software's growth-at-all-costs years, and now the AI shift upending all of software. Budgets that were loose became scrutinized. Renewals started needing a CFO's signature. The buyers we sell to, finance teams, were the very people doing the scrutinizing. So what held up across seven years of that? Retention, for one. Our gross revenue retention is 97%. Growth is more durable when you keep the business you have already earned, and a renewal from a finance buyer is not a sentimental decision. The platform keeps producing value in their numbers, or it doesn't. Our customers continue choosing the partnership year after year, and many introduce us to their peers. That is what four appearances represent to us. The list has our name on it. The trust behind that growth came from our customers. And behind every renewal was a team continuing to earn it by building, supporting, and solving alongside them. Over those seven years, finance teams have collected hundreds of billions of dollars in receivables through Tesorio. Through all of it, one belief has stayed the same: revenue ain't real till you get paid. What a lagging indicator can never tell you is what comes next. The work changed shape underneath those seven years. We started by building tools that helped AR teams move faster. Today we're building agents that take on more of the work across order-to-cash, so finance teams can spend more of their time on judgment and relationships. Agents handle the volume. People make the calls. We think the next generation of finance platforms won't just help teams manage the work. They'll increasingly take on the operational work alongside them. AI can amplify the work. It can't replace judgment.
